title: Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
authors: Qing-Bo Liu, Xin-Yi Chen, Xiangyang Li, Xingxing Li, Jinlong Yang
abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel. Then, via first-principles calculations, a screening of 90 two-dimensional ambidentate-ligand based square organometallic lattices leads to the identification of three altermagnetic materials, namely Fe(taz)2Cl2 (taz = 1,2,4- triazine), Co(app)2Cl2, and Fe(app)2Cl2 (app = 1,4-azaphosphinine), all of which possess 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in valence bands, as well as notable piezomagnetic behavior. This study paves the way for achieving direction-dependent fully spin-polarization in altermagnetic materials.
summary: This work proposes a novel chemical strategy using ambidentate ligands to construct 2D altermagnetic organometallic lattices. By engineering the electronic structure to feature coexisting dispersive and flat spin-split bands, the authors demonstrated the realization of 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in three specific materials. This paves the way for designing next-generation spintronic devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a feasible chemical strategy to design two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets that exhibit 100% spin polarization along a specific crystallographic direction, such as [110].
main_result: The authors successfully identified three promising organometallic candidates ($	ext{Fe}(	ext{taz})_2	ext{Cl}_2$, $	ext{Co}(	ext{app})_2	ext{Cl}_2$, and $	ext{Fe}(	ext{app})_2	ext{Cl}_2$) that realize this state, demonstrating direction-dependent full spin polarization in their valence bands.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling using a tight-binding (TB) approach with first-principles calculations (DFT/PBE+U) to screen and characterize the electronic and magnetic properties of candidate materials.
model_or_system: The physical system consists of 2D square lattice organometallic lattices built using ambidentate ligands. The theoretical framework involves a modified tight-binding Hamiltonian designed to capture the altermagnetic spin-splitting mechanism.
key_observables: 100% spin polarization along [110], spin-dependent transport ($\sigma_{xy}$), piezomagnetic response (net magnetic moment under strain), and the coexistence of dispersive and flat bands.
important_parameters: The key mechanism relies on the coexistence of a highly dispersive band in one spin channel and a flat band in the other, which suppresses transport in one spin channel.
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on the structural modification provided by ambidentate ligands, which breaks inversion symmetry and induces the necessary spin-splitting.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin-dependent transport mechanisms, showing how the combination of dispersive and flat bands leads to 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction. Band structures and spin-resolved conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$) are key diagnostic tools.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the challenge (designing 100% spin-polarized altermagnets) to proposing a chemical strategy (ambidentate ligands), detailing the theoretical model (TB Hamiltonian), presenting the screening workflow (90 candidates), and finally confirming the results with three specific, highly polarized materials.
why_interesting: The concept of altermagnetism and achieving perfect spin polarization via structural engineering in MOFs is highly relevant to spintronics and quantum materials research, bridging magnetism and electronic transport in a controllable solid-state manner.
